exercise.name: Barbell Step-Up
library_steps: Rest the bar on your upper back and face a sturdy box or bench.
Place one foot fully on the box and push through it to stand up.
Step down slowly with the same leg; switch legs after your set.
exercise.one_line_summary: A bar on the upper back, one foot flat on a ~0.4 m box; the lead leg straightens to stand on the box. Quadriceps does the most, glutes and hamstrings help.

setup.target: Box ~0.40 m high, the whole lead foot on it.
setup.why: Library step 2; SIM used a 45.72 cm box.

setup.target: High on the upper back, hands just outside the shoulders.

muscles.emg: Lateral step-up: vastus medialis obliquus above 45 % MVIC (EKS).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The rear leg launches the body.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Takes the work from the lead leg.

sources.citation: Ekstrom RA, Donatelli RA, Carp KC. 2007. Electromyographic analysis of core trunk, hip, and thigh muscles during 9 rehabilitation exercises. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther.
sources.what_it_gave: Lateral step-up and lunge: vastus medialis obliquus (quadriceps) above 45 % MVIC; gluteal and hamstring muscles also measured.

sources.citation: Simenz CJ, Garceau LR, Lutsch BN, Suchomel TJ, Ebben WP. 2010. Electromyographical analysis of lower extremity muscle activation during variations of the loaded step up exercise. ISBS Conference Proceedings Archive.
sources.what_it_gave: Loaded step-ups on a 45.72 cm (18 in) box: thigh and hip muscle activation across step-up variations.

sources.citation: Clark DR, Lambert MI, Hunter AM. 2012. Muscle activation in the loaded free barbell squat: a brief review. J Strength Cond Res.
sources.what_it_gave: Review of 18 squat EMG studies: prime-mover activation rises with load; stance width, hip rotation and front loading do not change activation much.
